findings.evidence: Line 36 is `#define INV3D_DRAG 1`, and the definition of `void syncScreen()` at line 303 sits inside the `#if INV3D_DRAG` block opened at line 289 and closed by `#endif` at line 332. Line 108 forward-declares `void syncScreen();` unconditionally, and it is called unconditionally from `loadIni()` at lines 118 and 140. With INV3D_DRAG set to 0 (the file's own documented toggle, line 36 comment) the declaration has no definition, so the build links with an unresolved `syncScreen` and the INI loader depends on a symbol that the flag removes.
findings.suggested_investigation: Compile Inventory3DViewport.cpp with -DINV3D_DRAG=0 (or temporarily edit line 36) and check for an undefined reference to syncScreen. Then check whether the screen-sync function should live outside the #if INV3D_DRAG block (lines 303-306 moved above line 289), or whether loadIni's calls at lines 118 and 140 should be guarded the same way.
findings.why_it_matters: The new syncScreen call sites were added in the uncommitted v2 change to loadIni, which is outside any INV3D_DRAG guard. Any non-drag build (the flag is documented as a switch back to no mouse polling) will fail at link time or, if the symbol is supplied elsewhere, silently drop the screen sync. The flag is a documented toggle, so the dependency is a portability regression.

findings.evidence: logf (lines 63-68) increments `++g_logLines` and returns when `g_logLines >= MaxLogLines`, but the new `logw` at lines 69-72 and `loge` at lines 73-76 call `KP_LOGV` directly with no counter. Warning sites that fire on every hover event are therefore uncapped, e.g. line 473 `logw("H2: slot unusable (panel=%08x)", panel)` and line 479/482 in ShowItem, which run per ShowItem call.
findings.suggested_investigation: Check whether KpLog itself rate-limits or caps lines (look at KpLog.h / KP_LOGV). If it does not, decide whether logw/loge should share the g_logLines counter (or a separate warn cap) and confirm by counting log lines from a session that repeatedly hovers an item whose slot is unusable (ShowItem, around lines 471-473).
findings.why_it_matters: The cap exists to stop the log from being starved or flooded. The ported warning paths sit on per-event code, so a persistent unusable-slot or out-of-range condition could emit unbounded lines into the core log file on every item hover, which the cap was meant to prevent.
